info.title: HRMS Platform
info.summary: HR, time, leave and hiring for multi-company groups
info.description:
The HRMS platform API: core HR, time and attendance, leave, approvals, KYC, recruitment and
reporting for multi-company groups. The web app uses this same API, so anything a user can do
in the app, an integration can do too.

## Quick start

1. **Sign in.** Call `POST /v1/auth/login` with the user's sign-in identifier (email, employee
   code or mobile number) and password:

   ```bash
   curl -X POST "$BASE_URL/v1/auth/login" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"identifier": "hr@example.com", "password": "••••••••"}'
   ```

   The response contains `access_token`, `expires_in` (seconds) and `user`. `user` holds the
   caller's roles, permissions and the companies they can see.

2. **Call the API** with that token in the `Authorization` header:

   ```bash
   curl "$BASE_URL/v1/employees?limit=50" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
   ```

3. **Sign in again when the token expires.** You'll get `401`. There is no refresh token.

**In this page:** run *Auth → Sign in* with **Try it out**, and the token is filled in for every
other request automatically. You can also paste a token into **Authorize** (top right).

## Authentication

| Who | Sign in with | Token works on |
|---|---|---|
| Employees, managers, HR, integrations | `POST /v1/auth/login` | all but `/v1/platform/*` |
| Platform operators | `POST /v1/platform/login` | `/v1/platform/*` only |

- **Your company is in the token.** The token decides which company's data you see. No header
  or parameter can switch it.
- **Company code.** Some employee codes or mobile numbers are used in more than one company.
  Signing in with one of these returns `409 COMPANY_REQUIRED`. Send the company code as
  `tenant` and try again.
- **Two-factor sign-in.** If the account uses an authenticator app, sign-in returns
  `401 MFA_REQUIRED`. Send the 6-digit code as `otp` and try again.
- **Password change.** A temporary password must be replaced before the API will work.
  Until then, calls return `403 PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED`. Call `POST /v1/auth/change-password`,
  and use the new token it returns.
- **Changing a password ends every session for that account.** Tokens issued before the
  change stop working at once.
- **Too many failed sign-ins** return `429` with a `Retry-After` header (in seconds).

**For integrations,** create a dedicated user account (*Users → Create a user account*). Give it
only the role it needs. Never use a person's own login.

## What a caller can see

What a call returns depends on the caller's roles:

- **Permissions** decide which actions are allowed (for example `leave.write`). Without the
  right permission, a call returns `403` with `Missing permission: <name>`. Where an endpoint
  declares its permission, the endpoint's description says so.
- **Scope** decides which records are visible: all companies, chosen companies, chosen
  departments, the caller's direct reports, or only the caller. List endpoints quietly leave
  out records outside the scope. Single-record endpoints return `403` or `404`.

`GET /v1/auth/me` shows the caller's roles, permissions and visible companies.

## Conventions

- **Base path.** Every endpoint is under `/v1`. New response fields can appear, so your client
  should ignore fields it doesn't recognise.
- **IDs** are opaque strings with a type prefix, for example `emp_…` (employment),
  `per_…` (person), `le_…` (legal entity), `ou_…` (department), `la_…` (leave application).
  Store them and send them back exactly as you got them. Don't parse them.
- **Dates** are `YYYY-MM-DD`, and **timestamps** are ISO 8601. "Today" and work dates follow
  the company's business day, not your clock.
- **Paging.** List endpoints that page take `limit` and `offset`. Each endpoint shows its
  default and maximum `limit`.
- **Request IDs.** Every response has an `X-Request-ID` header. You can send your own
  `X-Request-ID` (up to 64 characters: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:`, `-`) and it is used
  instead, which helps you trace a call across both systems.
  Include it when you report a problem.
- **API version.** The `X-App-Version` response header shows the deployed version.

## Errors

Every error has the same JSON body:

```json
{
  "detail": "Validation error on from_date: Input should be a valid date",
  "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
  "request_id": "req_01J9...",
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "Validation error on from_date: Input should be a valid date",
    "details": [
      {"field": "from_date", "message": "Input should be a valid date", "type": "date_parsing"}
    ],
    "request_id": "req_01J9...",
    "timestamp": "2026-10-06T09:30:00+00:00"
  }
}
```

Use `code` in your program logic. `detail` is a message for people and its wording can change.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `400` | The request is not valid for the record's current state |
| `401` | Missing, expired or invalid token. Codes: `MFA_REQUIRED`, `MFA_INVALID` |
| `403` | Not allowed. Codes: `PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED`, `MFA_SETUP_REQUIRED` |
| `404` | Not found, or outside the caller's scope |
| `409` | Conflicts with existing data (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `COMPANY_REQUIRED`) |
| `422` | A field failed validation. `error.details` lists each field |
| `429` | Rate-limited. Wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After` |
| `5xx` | Server error. Retry with backoff, and quote `request_id` if it continues |

## The schema

The machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 schema is at [`/openapi.json`](/openapi.json). You can generate
a typed client from it, for example
`npx openapi-typescript $BASE_URL/openapi.json -o hrms-api.d.ts`.
The same reference, as one long page, is at [`/redoc`](/redoc).

post.description:
Works even while a password change is being *required* (imported and
admin-reset accounts). Every token issued before this call is rejected
from now on, so the response carries a fresh one — the caller stays signed
in, anyone else holding the old password or token does not.

post.summary: Register a brand-new company as its own isolated tenant
post.description:
This is NOT "add a sister company" (POST /v1/org/legal-entities) — that
adds a legal entity inside the CALLER's existing tenant, and requires
already being signed in as that tenant's admin. This is a different
tenant altogether: a new isolation boundary with its own roles, its own
first company, and a first SUPER_ADMIN login that can never see (and is
never visible to) SFPL Group or any other tenant. See also
POST /v1/platform/companies, which a platform admin uses to do the same
thing (or link a company under an EXISTING tenant instead) without
becoming that tenant's user themselves.

Anonymous, so it is rate-limited per client IP (settings.register_max_per_hour)
and can be switched off entirely (HRMS_ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION=false) for
deployments where tenants are only created from the platform console.

at login — role (and status) are resolved fresh from the DB per request
everywhere else in this router, and the UI should match: if another
admin promotes or demotes this account, or a client's cached login
predates a field being added here, the very next page load reflects the
current truth instead of a stale login response.

post.summary: Cancel a scheduled (or failed) personnel action
post.description:
**Requires permission:** `people.write`

A future-dated action (a separation, a transfer, ...) applies by itself on
its effective date, so there has to be a way to stop one that was entered
wrongly. Only SCHEDULED and FAILED actions can be cancelled — an APPLIED one
is history; correct it with a new action instead.

**Requires permission:** `dashboard.hr`

Every figure here is limited to the employees the caller's dashboard.hr grants
cover (`emp_clause`, always against the alias `e`): an HR manager scoped to one
company sees that company's headcount, KYC status, tenure and departments — not
the group's. (The clause used to be built for the alias `employments` and reused
in queries that alias the table `e`, which made every entity-scoped HR manager and
accountant get a 500, and several aggregates skipped the clause altogether.)

Each section runs only when asked for, and a query shared by several sections (KYC
counts, the distributions) runs once per request.

get.description:
One row per leave type with an active balance, summed from the ledger for
the given financial year (the employee's own, via their legal entity's
financial_year_start_month). carry_forward_days is the FY's opening
balance; allocated_days is what was credited (accrual + grants) during
the FY itself — the two used to be two separate stored numbers, they're
now two different aggregates over the same ledger rows. A type with no
ledger activity yet in this FY (e.g. never accrued) doesn't appear —
same as when this read the old, now-retired leave_balances table.

post.description:
**Requires permission:** `leave.write`

One-shot manual credit or debit to an employee's leave balance, for cases
the normal flows don't cover: seeding an opening balance carried over
from a previous system (kind="OPENING"), or correcting a mistake
(kind="ADJUSTMENT"). Posts a single transaction through the same ledger
every other write path uses — the two kinds differ only in which ledger
column and audit label they post under; the balance math is identical.

post.description:
**Requires permission:** `leave.write`

Credits every eligible employee's bucket, per resolved entitlement, for
every paid or comp-off leave type. "Resolved entitlement" is an explicit
LeaveBucketPolicy if one applies to that employee, else the leave type's
own days_per_year/accrual_enabled fields — a tenant that's never touched
Policy -> Leave policies gets exactly today's behaviour, just posted
through the ledger. Idempotency is a journal lookup (an ACCRUAL
transaction already dated this exact period) rather than a separate
marker field, so this is safe to call more than once for the same or an
earlier period; it does not backfill a month that was skipped by
mistake. Meant to be triggered by an external cron; there is no in-app
scheduler (see RUNBOOK.md).

post.description:
**Requires permission:** `leave.write`

For every (employment, bucket) with ledger activity in fy_year: cap the
FY's closing balance at the resolved policy's max_carry_forward_days
(posting a LAPSE for the excess) or leave it uncapped if no cap resolves
— the remainder simply IS next FY's opening, the same way every other
month-to-month transition already works, via the ordinary prior-row
lookup in get_or_create_ledger_row/the forward cascade. No separate
CARRY_FORWARD transaction is posted: doing so on top of the LAPSE would
double the balance (CARRY_FORWARD's effect is additive), and posting it
on the new FY's row instead only works when that row doesn't already
exist (an advance-dated hold can create it first) — the LAPSE + cascade
path handles both cases correctly with one transaction.

Idempotent per (employment, bucket): skipped if a YEAR_END-referenced
transaction already exists dated this FY's closing month.

get.description: Birthdays and completed work anniversaries in the signed-in employee's own company, plus personal wishes. The company comes from the caller's employment; no employee or company selector is accepted. Available to every authenticated tenant user, without HR dashboard access. Accounts without a current employment get empty lists. Dates use the tenant timezone; February 29 is observed on February 28 in non-leap years. Birth dates, birth years, ages and contact details are never returned.

replace.title: Replace

KycAccessLogEntry.description: One time someone other than the employee opened their KYC dossier or a document.

LeaveApplicationSummary.description: Counts for everyone in the caller's scope — for dashboards, without fetching the list.

LegalEntityUpdate.description: All fields optional — only what's sent gets changed (and audited).

LibraryHoliday.title: LibraryHoliday
LibraryHoliday.description: A holiday on the year's holiday list, and the calendars that include it.

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest
LoginRequest.description:
`identifier` is an email address, employee code or mobile number. The legacy
payload keys (email / username / phone / mobile / user / emp_id) are still
accepted so existing clients keep working.

MyProfileUpdate.title: MyProfileUpdate
MyProfileUpdate.description:
Every field optional and unset-vs-null aware (PATCH semantics via
model_dump(exclude_unset=True) in the router) — sending a field clears
it to null, omitting it leaves the current value untouched.

OrgUnitUpdate.title: OrgUnitUpdate
OrgUnitUpdate.description:
Renaming/recoding only — moving a unit to a different parent, company or
location is a structural change, not covered here (create a new unit and
migrate assignments, or ask for that as its own endpoint if it's needed).

PasswordReset.title: PasswordReset
PasswordReset.description: A temporary password. The user is made to replace it at their next sign-in.

changes.title: Changes
changes.description: Changed fields and new values; use typed IDs for references.

PersonnelActionCreate.title: PersonnelActionCreate
PersonnelActionCreate.description: POST /v1/personnel-actions — the only write path for employment changes.

PreferencesUpdate.title: PreferencesUpdate
PreferencesUpdate.description: Only the fields sent are changed.

StagesUpdate.title: StagesUpdate
StagesUpdate.description: The whole pipeline in display order. Stages left out are deactivated.

TenantRegister.title: TenantRegister
TenantRegister.description:
Registering a brand-new company here means a brand-new TENANT — a
completely separate isolation boundary from any existing tenant (e.g.
SFPL Group), not another legal entity inside one. Adding a sister
company to an existing group is POST /v1/org/legal-entities instead,
which requires already being signed in as that tenant's admin.

TodayStatusResponse.title: TodayStatusResponse
TodayStatusResponse.description: What the employee sees when they open the punch clock.

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description: INACTIVE blocks sign-in (and every existing token) at once; ACTIVE restores it.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: The body of every error response. Use `code` in program logic, and show `detail` to people.

details.description: For validation errors: one entry per field.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Sign in, sign out, change password, two-factor setup, and the signed-in user's profile, roles and permissions (`/v1/auth/me`).

tags.name: Users
tags.description: User accounts (logins) and the roles that grant permissions and scope.

tags.name: Preferences
tags.description: The signed-in user's own settings, such as theme and default dashboard.

tags.name: Organisation
tags.description: Company structure: legal entities (companies), locations, departments (org units), jobs and employee ID schemes. Each has a change history.

tags.name: People
tags.description: Persons (the individual) and employments (their job in a company). An employee is identified by the employment ID (`emp_…`). Personnel actions handle transfers, promotions and separations, and can be dated in the future.

tags.name: Onboarding
tags.description: Checklist templates, and onboarding cases for new hires.

tags.name: Employee KYC
tags.description: Identity and bank details, and their documents. Employees maintain their own (`/me`), and HR verifies them. Every time someone opens a record or document, it is logged.

tags.name: Time & Attendance
tags.description: Punches, daily attendance, overtime review, daily analysis and the HR attendance register.

tags.name: Attendance Corrections
tags.description: Employee requests to fix missed or wrong punches. They go through the approval workflow.

tags.name: Holiday calendars
tags.description: A shared holiday list, and holiday calendars built from it. Calendars are assigned to companies, departments or individual employees.

tags.name: HR Policies
tags.description: Attendance and shift policy templates, their assignments, and the policy that applies to an employee on a given date.

tags.name: Leave Management
tags.description: Leave types, policy sets and buckets, balances, the leave ledger, applications, and how an application is approved or cancelled. Also covers comp-off, encashment, accrual runs and year-end close.

tags.name: Approval workflows
tags.description: Approval flows, the approver's inbox, decisions and delegations. Leave, corrections and recruitment openings all use these flows.

tags.name: Recruitment
tags.description: Job openings and their approval, the hiring pipeline stages, candidates and resumes, applications, and turning an application into a hire.

tags.name: Dashboard
tags.description: Dashboards for each role, and each user's saved layout.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Saved report definitions, the columns and filters each module offers, and running a report.

tags.name: Platform
tags.description: For platform operators only: tenants, platform admins and the audit log. These endpoints need a **platform** token from `POST /v1/platform/login`. A tenant user's token is rejected.
